data.transcript:
WEBVTT


00:00:00.020 --> 00:00:01.540
Your tariffs are illegal. They're not.

00:00:01.541 --> 00:00:03.461
The president can charge whatever country he wants.

00:00:03.462 --> 00:00:05.021
But he used this law to implement them

00:00:05.022 --> 00:00:06.301
and didn't have the power to do so.

00:00:06.302 --> 00:00:08.181
Fine. Then I'll do new tariffs under different laws.

00:00:08.182 --> 00:00:10.261
A 10% global tariff, effective immediately.

00:00:10.262 --> 00:00:11.861
Also, according to the Constitution,

00:00:11.862 --> 00:00:13.061
tariffs are considered taxes,

00:00:13.062 --> 00:00:14.581
which have to be approved by Congress.

00:00:14.582 --> 00:00:16.801
They're not taxes. The Constitution disagrees.

00:00:16.802 --> 00:00:19.301
First time Congress taxed people was with a law for a tariff.

00:00:19.302 --> 00:00:20.781
I'm ashamed of certain members of the court.

00:00:20.782 --> 00:00:21.821
They're a disgrace to our nation.

00:00:21.822 --> 00:00:23.181
Hang on. This feels like a big circle.

00:00:23.182 --> 00:00:25.341
Why is this significant? This ruling has huge stakes.

00:00:25.342 --> 00:00:27.261
Tariffs affect trillions of dollars in trade.

00:00:27.262 --> 00:00:30.661
The government collected nearly $134 billion by mid December.

00:00:30.662 --> 00:00:32.821
So what happens now? Isn't the state of the union on Tuesday?

00:00:32.822 --> 00:00:34.781
Yes, and the Supreme Court justices sometimes go.

00:00:34.782 --> 00:00:36.701
But two of the three justices Trump appointed

00:00:36.702 --> 00:00:37.941
sided against him in the ruling.

00:00:37.942 --> 00:00:39.621
So he said, I couldn't care less if they come,

00:00:39.622 --> 00:00:40.858
because the Supreme Court said.
